cat > .github/workflows/triage.yml <<'EOF'
---
name: triage

# pull_request_target gives pull requests from forks a token that can comment
# and label. It runs with this repository's privileges, so this workflow must
# never check out, build or run anything from the pull request.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Triage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      # Pull request data is attacker-controlled. Pass it through env and quote
      # it; never put a ${{ }} expression inside the script.
      - name: Label and welcome
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          gh api --silent "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/labels" \
            -f 'labels[]=needs-triage'

          # The title goes in an indented code block, so that mentions, links
          # and other Markdown in it stay inert.
          title=$(printf '%s' "$PR_TITLE" | tr '\r\n' '  ')
          body=$(printf 'Welcome, @%s, and thank you for your contribution!\n\nSummary of this pull request:\n\n    %s\n' \
            "$PR_AUTHOR" "$title")

          gh api --silent "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" \
            -f "body=$body"
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Triage

When a pull request is opened, including one from a fork, the
[triage workflow](.github/workflows/triage.yml):

- applies the `needs-triage` label
- posts a comment that welcomes the contributor by username and repeats the
  pull request title

Setup: create the `needs-triage` label in the repository (once), for example
with `gh label create needs-triage`.

The workflow only runs on `opened`, so editing, reopening or pushing to a pull
request does not post another comment. Changes to the workflow take effect once
they are on the base branch, not from the pull request that proposes them.

### Maintaining it safely

The workflow uses `pull_request_target`, because the `pull_request` token is
read-only for forks. That means it runs with write access while handling input
from people you may not trust:

- Do not add a step that checks out, builds or runs code from the pull request.
  Tests belong in the [ci workflow](.github/workflows/ci.yml).
- Do not insert `${{ github.event.* }}` values into a `run` script. Pass them
  through `env` and quote the variables.
- Keep the permissions to what labelling and commenting need
  (`pull-requests: write`).
EOF
actionlint && echo actionlint-ok; which zizmor && zizmor .github/workflows
# run the script with a stub gh and a hostile title
d=$(mktemp -d); printf '#!/bin/sh\nfor a in "$@"; do printf "[%%s]\\n" "$a"; done\n' > $d/gh; chmod +x $d/gh
python3 -I -c 'import yaml,sys;print(yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))["jobs"]["triage"]["steps"][0]["run"])' .github/workflows/triage.yml > $d/s.sh
PATH=$d:$PATH REPO=o/r PR_NUMBER=1 PR_AUTHOR=octocat PR_TITLE='"; $(touch '$d'/pwned) `id` @org/team %s
second' bash -eo pipefail $d/s.sh; ls $d; rm -rf $d; git status --short

content.text:
I added the triage workflow in `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and documented it in a new Triage section of the README. Nothing is committed, and it hasn't run on GitHub.

**What it does:** when a pull request is opened, it applies `needs-triage`, then posts this comment:

> Welcome, @username, and thank you for your contribution!
>
> Summary of this pull request:
>
> `<the PR title>`

**Forks:** it uses `pull_request_target`, because the ordinary `pull_request` trigger gives fork PRs a read-only token that can't comment or label. The catch is that it runs with write access while handling text from strangers, so I limited it:
- It never checks out or runs code from the pull request.
- Its only permission is `pull-requests: write`.
- The title and username reach the script as environment variables, so a title can't inject shell commands.
- The title is shown as a code block, so an `@mention` or link in it does nothing.

**Checks:**
- `actionlint` passes.
- I ran the script with a stand-in for `gh` and a hostile title containing quotes, `$(...)`, backticks, a mention and a line break. The title came through as plain text and nothing in it ran.
- `zizmor` reports one high-severity finding, `dangerous-triggers`, because it flags any use of `pull_request_target`. That is expected here. I didn't suppress it, so if you add `zizmor` to CI you'll need an ignore comment for it.

**Before you rely on it:**
1. Create the label once: `gh label create needs-triage`.
2. Merge the workflow into `main`. `pull_request_target` uses the base branch's copy, so it won't run on the PR that adds it.
3. Open a test PR from a fork and check that both the label and comment appear. This is the only real test of the fork behaviour and token permissions.
